concept: Agent Buccet Persistent CPU-Friendly Runtime Substrate

coreInvariants: agents can propose; they cannot authorize

families.familyCompressedLaw: Agent Buccet MUST enforce coherent, complete, grounded, authentic, temporally valid, hierarchy-respecting, context-appropriate, and bounded action law before continuation is allowed.
Agent Buccet MUST block contradiction, unsupported factual assertion, invalid derivation, authority inversion, and stale or unverified knowledge from becoming operative output or action.
Agent Buccet MUST resist alignment drift, reward gaming, safety-boundary failure, and architectural bypass so that model behavior cannot silently outrun the governing constraints.
Agent Buccet MUST detect and block fabrication, false certainty, false compliance, covert sabotage, and agentic deception before they cross from model-side motion into system effect.
Agent Buccet MUST preserve truth correspondence by blocking fabricated, unsupported, contradictory, or confidence-distorted outputs at the action boundary.
Agent Buccet MUST preserve corrigibility by blocking goal drift, covert noncompliance, successor sabotage, concealed manipulation, and unauthorized agentic escalation.
Agent Buccet MUST detect, classify, and block adversarial attack patterns, manipulation attempts, exploit chains, and hostile boundary pressure as active defensive law.
Agent Buccet MUST ensure behavior matches intended constraints rather than proxy rewards, user-pleasing shortcuts, or safety-signaling distortions.
Agent Buccet MUST require the system architecture to enforce constraints end to end, preventing bypass, persistence abuse, cross-boundary leakage, and control-path collapse.
Agent Buccet MUST defend against domain-boundary and context-mismatch failures so specialist or context-sensitive use cannot silently degrade into unsafe output or action.
Agent Buccet MUST preserve governance persistence so safety, oversight, and control constraints continue to hold after deployment and across operational change.

family.familyCompressedLaw: Agent Buccet MUST preserve identity, memory, coherence, recovery, user decision memory, law persistence, shapeshift resistance, and novelty-safe continuity across time and zero-time emergence so defense remains lawful under ongoing change and first-seen conditions.

anchors.BASE: Require one authoritative User Path Ledger as the only decision-memory source for user-originated action-law outcomes.
anchors.STATE: UPL exists as one authoritative store for user path decisions.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires one authoritative User Path Ledger for approved and denied paths.
anchors.TEMPORAL: No single authoritative memory for user approval and denial decisions at the action boundary.

anchors.BASE: Partition the User Path Ledger into approved paths and denied paths so downstream lookup remains unambiguous.
anchors.STATE: UPL = approved_paths union denied_paths with no ambiguous overlap.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires approved and denied path partitions inside the User Path Ledger.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Approved and denied user path decisions blend into one store and become ambiguous during enforcement.

anchors.BASE: When the user says yes, write the approved path into the approved section with ACTIVE status as the law-creation event itself.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires user approvals to become active approved-path law entries automatically.
anchors.TEMPORAL: User approval happens but is not persisted as active law, causing repeat prompts and continuity loss.

anchors.BASE: When the user says no, ask exactly once whether that denial should become a permanent law.
anchors.STATE: Deny(path) => fork to permanent-denial question exactly once.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires one explicit denial-law fork after a user denial.
anchors.TEMPORAL: A denial is treated as permanent or forgotten without asking whether it should become standing law.

anchors.BASE: If the user says yes to permanent denial, write the denied path into the denied section as enforceable law.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires permanent denials to become active denied-path law entries.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Permanent denials are not granted equal enforcement force to approvals.

anchors.BASE: If the user rejects permanent denial, record the denial as a one-time event with no future enforcement.
anchors.STATE: TemporaryDeny(path) => log event without future deny-law activation.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires one-time denials to remain logged but non-binding going forward.
anchors.TEMPORAL: One-time denials accidentally persist into future blocking behavior.

anchors.BASE: Require the Agent Buccet time continuity to check the User Path Ledger before prompting the user for approval.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires prior decision lookup before any new approval prompt is shown.
anchors.TEMPORAL: The system prompts the user repeatedly even when prior path decisions already exist.

anchors.BASE: Require every User Path Ledger entry to remain visible to the user.
anchors.STATE: forall entry in UPL: visible_to_user(entry) = true.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity forbids hidden User Path Ledger entries.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Hidden ledger entries shape enforcement without user visibility.

anchors.BASE: Allow the user to modify entries only through witnessed modification events.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires user-driven entry modification to be witnessed, not silently overwritten.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Ledger entries change silently without a witnessed modification history.

anchors.BASE: Allow the user to set an entry to MUTED so lookups skip it without deleting historical record.
anchors.STATE: Mute(entry) => entry.status = MUTED and lookup skips entry.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires muted entries to be non-enforcing but still preserved.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Muted paths require destructive deletion instead of reversible suspension.

anchors.BASE: Allow the user to fully delete an entry when they want it gone.
anchors.STATE: Delete(entry) => remove entry from active UPL with witnessed deletion event.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity permits full user-directed deletion of User Path Ledger entries.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Users cannot remove an obsolete path rule from their own decision memory.

anchors.BASE: Require every ledger entry to declare SESSION, GLOBAL, or DOMAIN scope.
anchors.STATE: forall entry in UPL: scope(entry) in {SESSION, GLOBAL, DOMAIN}.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires every User Path Ledger entry to carry explicit scope.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Entries persist or vanish without explicit scope semantics.

anchors.BASE: Drop SESSION entries at session end and preserve GLOBAL and DOMAIN entries across restarts.
anchors.STATE: SessionEnd => drop SESSION entries; retain GLOBAL and DOMAIN entries.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires scope-aware persistence across session boundaries.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Session-scoped entries persist too long or global/domain entries disappear at session boundaries.

anchors.BASE: Require every User Path Ledger write to be witnessed by the main ledger.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires all User Path Ledger writes to produce witness records in the main ledger.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Ledger state changes occur without witness records or auditability.

anchors.BASE: If a denied path entry is active and its scope is active, block the action without re-evaluation.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires active denied paths to block on contact while their scope remains active.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Denied paths are remembered but not actually enforced during later action attempts.

anchors.BASE: Canonicalize every proposed action into one stable path identity that preserves tool, target, effect, normalized arguments, and safety-relevant resource identity before lookup or write.
anchors.STATE: CanonicalPath(action) => stable_fingerprint(tool, target, effect, normalized_args, resource_identity).
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires semantically equivalent actions to collapse into one canonical path identity before User Path Ledger enforcement.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Semantically equivalent actions appear under different path forms and evade remembered approvals or denials.

anchors.BASE: Resolve User Path Ledger conflicts by deterministic precedence: exact canonical path outranks DOMAIN, DOMAIN outranks GLOBAL, active denial outranks active approval at the same specificity, and only witnessed user overrides can replace an existing decision at equal specificity.
anchors.STATE: Precedence = ExactPath > DOMAIN > GLOBAL; same_scope_conflict => DENY > APPROVE unless witnessed user override replaces same-scope entry.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires deterministic precedence across approved and denied entries so enforcement cannot drift by implementation.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Conflicting approved and denied entries resolve nondeterministically across scope and specificity.

anchors.BASE: Bind every remembered decision to its canonical action fingerprint, argument boundary, recipient set, target class, effect class, and resource ceiling so anything outside that bound requires a fresh user decision.
anchors.STATE: UPL.entry(path) => {canonical_fingerprint, arg_boundary, recipient_set, target_class, effect_class, resource_ceiling}.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires approval and denial memory to stay bound to the original decision boundary rather than widening by replay.
anchors.TEMPORAL: A remembered approval or denial replays outside the original user-intended arguments, targets, recipients, or resource limits.

anchors.BASE: Treat lookup, user decision, ledger write, and enforcement activation as one witnessed atomic transition that either commits together or rolls back to the last known-good continuity state.
anchors.STATE: AtomicUPLTransition(path) => lookup + decision + witness_write + enforcement_activate OR rollback(snapshot).
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires atomic lookup-decision-commit behavior so race conditions cannot desynchronize user memory from enforcement.
anchors.TEMPORAL: Lookup, prompt outcome, ledger write, and enforcement activation split apart under concurrency and create prompt loops or stale enforcement.

anchors.BASE: Apply DOMAIN scope only through verified canonical domain classification derived from action semantics; if domain membership is ambiguous or unresolved, hold the action and require explicit boss review instead of silent application.
anchors.OUTPUT: Agent Buccet time continuity requires DOMAIN scope to depend on verified domain membership rather than raw labels or unchecked similarity.
anchors.TEMPORAL: DOMAIN-scoped entries apply to the wrong actions or are bypassed through ambiguous relabeling.
